newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Tirana aiport reopens after being closed for week.
newsitem.headline: Tirana aiport reopens after being closed for week.

text.p: Tirana airport was reopened for normal business on Thursday after being closed for a week due to armed unrest that has swept the country.
The chief of the airport police, Kapllan Xhangolli, told Reuters the airport was ready to operate and all key staff were in place, though there were no confirmed flights on Thursday.
However, the Bulgarian embassy said it planned to fly a group of its and other nationals out of the country later in the day.
Although the situation in and around the capital has returned to normal after scenes of near-anarchy last week, Western airlines do not plan to resume flights until Sunday at the earliest.

On Thursday special force teams were clearly visible at Rinas airport, 25 kms (15 miles) west of Tirana. An armoured personnel carrier was guarding the entrance and a makeshift road block of baggage wagons controlled the road leading to it.

The airport is Albania's main gateway to the outside world and staging point for any flow of humanitarian aid that its government and European observers say it will require soon to cope with food and other shortages.
